newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-SFE 1996 trade shows international focus.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-SFE 1996 trade shows international focus.

text.p: Total turnover on the Sydney Futures Exchange (SFE) slipped slightly to 25.53 million contracts in calendar 1996 from 25.75 million in 1995, SFE figures released on Wednesday show.
The total includes both futures and options as well as trades on both the SFE floor and the after hours SYCOM system.
Key trends in 1996 included strong growth in options with trading volume up 36 percent to a record 3.2 million contracts, SFE said.
SYCOM trading rose by 30 percent to a record 3.1 million contracts representing 12 percent of turnover, SFE said.
SFE chief executive Les Hosking said in a statement the strategy to develop a 24 hour market through SYCOM, Overnight Options and international linkages bore substantial returns during 1996.
This had allowed overseas investors in Australia's bond and share markets to react to influences on Australian markets during their own daylight working hours.

The SFE's daily turnover increased substantially in the second half of 1996, reflecting the two interest rate cuts announced by the Reserve Bank of Australia after 18 months of unchanged official rates, he said.
SFE said trading in All Ordinaries share price index futures rose by 8.1 percent to 2.68 million in 1996.

Turnover of 90-day bank bills futures fell by 19.4 percent to 4.98 million, three-year bonds rose 4.4 percent to 9.21 million and 10-year bonds fell by 7.4 percent to 5.32 million, the SFE figures show.
Trading in greasy wool futures jumped by 57.4 percent to 7,554 contracts. The new wheat futures contract was not far behind, with 6,482 contracts changing hands.
A total 54,463 share futures traded in 1996, down strongly from 111,696 in 1995.
Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, MIM Holdings Ltd and Westpac Banking Corp were the three most heavily-traded share futures.
SFE said trading on the New Zealand Futures and Options Exchange rose by 24 percent.
